cues.text: Hello, Mr Thompson. May I speak to you for a minute?
cues.speaker: JONES

cues.text: Of course. Please come in.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: I’m Alexandra Jones. I’m studying Sustainability here at the university and I heard about the summer course that you offer every year.
cues.speaker: JONES

cues.text: I was considering joining the course and wanted to ask you some questions about it.
cues.speaker: JONES

cues.text: Yes, of course, please fire away.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Has the course been effective in improving the environment?
cues.speaker: JONES

cues.text: Yes, absolutely. We have seen great results.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Last year we planted a small field of trees and we have been measuring their oxygen outputs to see the benefits that they have provided to the environment.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Since we were regulated by law last month, we are now able to hugely enhance our efforts.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Our current goal is to introduce a lot more tree species to the plot so that we can establish a complex habitat and compare the benefits of each species.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: In order to do this we need to get a lot more students involved in the project, so I am very pleased to hear about your interest.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Well, the project sounds fascinating. I would definitely like to be involved,
cues.speaker: JONES

cues.text: Absolutely. Over the years we have received funding from private investors and from selling shares, but the biggest improvement in our research came from a government fund that we received in the first year.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: This has greatly improved the organisation and we have since won prizes for our research.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Wow, how impressive!
cues.speaker: JONES

cues.text: Yes, it is of the utmost importance to our organisation that we find a way to repair the terrible damage that has been done to the environment by the human species.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: This is no small undertaking and our resources still need management, but from reports taken of our studies we have found that teachers and students have greatly benefitted from field trips to the tree plantation.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Yes, I visited the plantation myself on a field trip two years ago and I found myself greatly impressed by it.
cues.speaker: JONES

cues.text: We have received a lot of feedback from visiting groups telling us how impressed teachers, researchers and students alike have been during their visits.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Due to the educational facilities that we have carefully structured, I know that the visits are useful and engaging for students and that their experience is particularly special.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: So what is the particular focus of the organisation and the reports that it provides?
cues.speaker: JONES

cues.text: I am personally very interested in soil erosion, so I knew that I definitely wanted to focus some of the report on this area.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Before I set up the organisation, I looked up information on what areas were currently being researched and I found that there were already studies into air pollution and water pollution.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: I obviously wanted to find a unique area to research and so these were no good.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: I was tempted to look into the background of overgrazing, Q26 but the impacts of forest exploitation are far more devastating and very little research has been carried out on this subject, so I decided that this should also form some focus for the report.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Yes, that makes sense. What have you found to be the greatest benefits of the activities carried out by the organisation?
cues.speaker: JONES

cues.text: I have found that the greatest benefits are not the ones that anyone can learn from a book, like how to collect data, but more importantly are life lessons that one can gain only from experience.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Students who have partaken in the summer course have massively enhanced their confidence, which will prove invaluable for the rest of their lifetime.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: The people who partake in the summer course already know the importance of environmental protection, so it is not important that we spend time teaching them this.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Students instead benefit from learning the importance of punctuality, as each day they have to wake up early to make sure that they are not late for their practical experience sessions.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: If I decide to attend the summer course, what will I be doing for the rest of the time when no activities are going on?
cues.speaker: JONES

cues.text: Well, we unfortunately don’t yet have a library on site, so you would be unable to read reference books although you are obviously welcome to bring some books of your own with you.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: We offer a range of fun hobbies, such as games and painting, for students to participate in outside of their classes. So you could participate in one of these activities.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: We do not offer tutorials outside of the scheduled classes, however you are free to interview teachers and ask them any questions you may have about the research.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: Well, the course sounds fantastic. I would definitely like to participate during the summer.
cues.speaker: JONES

cues.text: Thank you so much for your help.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON

cues.text: No problem at all, here is a form with all of the details. I look forward to seeing you there.
cues.speaker: MR THOMPSON
